6565.etyen:
Compound of blomst (“flower”) + løk (“bulb”), with the first element in the combining form blomster-, literally “flower bulb”.
The first element preserves the older stem represented by blomster (“flower, bloom”), from Old Norse blómstr (“flower”). The shorter singular blomst arose through reinterpretation of blomster as a plural. NAOB considers transmission of the shorter form through Danish blomst, from Old Danish blomstær, likely in most cases, while also allowing an Old Norse origin. The precise earlier formation of blómstr is uncertain.

1004709.etyen:
A Norwegian farm name and habitational surname. Several Norwegian farms bear the name, and the etymology varies by locality. The Holstad farms in Ås are from Old Norse Hávarðsstaðir, from the genitive singular of the male given name Hávarðr + staðir (“farmsteads, dwellings”), literally “Hávarðr’s farmsteads”.
Other farms called Holstad or Hølstad may instead have a first element from a different personal name or from hóll (“hill”). The second element staðir is the plural of staðr (“place, stead”), from Proto-Germanic *stadiz (“place, stead”), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“to stand”).
